<STRUCT_0001>
This is where we define algebraic stacks and make some very elementary
observations. The general philosophy will be to have no separation
conditions whatsoever and add those conditions necessary to make lemmas,
propositions, theorems true/provable. Thus the notions discussed here
differ slightly from those in other places in the literature, e.g.,
<REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
This chapter is not an introduction to algebraic stacks.
For an informal discussion of algebraic stacks, please take a look at
Introducing Algebraic Stacks, Section
<REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0001>
The conventions we use in this chapter are the same as those in the
chapter on algebraic spaces. For convenience we repeat them here.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Note that any fpqc covering is a universal effective
epimorphism, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0001>.
Hence the topology on <MATH_0001>
is weaker than the canonical topology and all representable presheaves
are sheaves.

<STRUCT_0001>
We use the letters <MATH_0001> to indicate schemes.
We use the letters <MATH_0002> to indicate
categories (fibred, fibred in groupoids, stacks, ...)
over <MATH_0003>. We use small case letters
<MATH_0004>, <MATH_0005> for functors such as <MATH_0006>
over <MATH_0007>.
We use capital <MATH_0008>, <MATH_0009>, <MATH_0010> for algebraic spaces over <MATH_0011>, and more
generally for presheaves of sets on <MATH_0012>.
(In future chapters we will revert to using also <MATH_0013>, <MATH_0014>, etc
for algebraic spaces.)

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
The reason for these choices is that we want to clearly distinguish between
the different types of objects in this chapter, to build the foundations.

<STRUCT_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme contained in <MATH_0002>.
The basic object of study in this chapter will be a
category fibred in groupoids
<MATH_0003>, see
Categories, Definition <REF_0001>.
We will often simply say ``let <MATH_0004> be a category fibred
in groupoids over <MATH_0005>'' to indicate
this situation. A <MATH_0006>-morphism <MATH_0007> of categories
fibred in groupoids over <MATH_0008> will be a <MATH_0009>-morphism
in the <MATH_0010>-category of categories fibred in groupoids over
<MATH_0011>, see
Categories,
Definition <REF_0002>.
It is simply a functor <MATH_0012> over
<MATH_0013>.
We recall this is really a <MATH_0014>-category and that all <MATH_0015>-fibre products
exist.

<STRUCT_0001>
<LOCKED_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition <REF_0001>.
Then <MATH_0002> is a universal effective epimorphism
in the category of schemes, see
Sites, Definition <REF_0002>.
In other words, every representable functor on the category of schemes
satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology, see
Topologies, Definition <REF_0003>.
<STRUCT_0002>

A <TEXTITOPEN_0001>big fppf site<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> is any site <MATH_0001> as in
Sites, Definition <REF_0001> constructed as follows:
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> Choose any set of schemes <MATH_0002>, and any set of fppf coverings
<MATH_0003> among these schemes.
<STRUCT_0004> As underlying category take any category <MATH_0004>
constructed as in Sets, Lemma <REF_0002>
starting with the set <MATH_0005>.
<STRUCT_0005> Choose any set of coverings as in
Sets, Lemma <REF_0003> starting with the
category <MATH_0006> and the class of fppf coverings,
and the set <MATH_0007> chosen above.
<STRUCT_0006>
<STRUCT_0007>

<STRUCT_0001>
<LOCKED_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be a big fppf
site containing <MATH_0003>.
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> The <TEXTITOPEN_0001>big fppf site of <MATH_0004><TEXTITCLOSE_0001>, denoted
<MATH_0005>, is the site <MATH_0006>
introduced in Sites, Section <REF_0001>.
<STRUCT_0004> The <TEXTITOPEN_0002>big affine fppf site of <MATH_0007><TEXTITCLOSE_0002>, denoted
<MATH_0008>, is the full subcategory of
<MATH_0009> whose objects are affine <MATH_0010>.
A covering of <MATH_0011> is any covering
<MATH_0012> of <MATH_0013> which is a
standard fppf covering.

selected.fragment:
\noindent
The conventions we use in this chapter are the same as those in the
chapter on algebraic spaces. For convenience we repeat them here.

\medskip\noindent
We work in a suitable big fppf site $\Sch_{fppf}$
as in Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-big-fppf-site}.
So, if not explicitly stated otherwise all schemes will be objects
of $\Sch_{fppf}$. We discuss what changes if you change the big
fppf site in
Section \ref{section-change-big-site}.

\medskip\noindent
We will always work relative to a base $S$ contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
And we will then work with the big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-big-small-fppf}.
The absolute case can be recovered by taking
$S = \Spec(\mathbf{Z})$.

\medskip\noindent
If $U, T$ are schemes over $S$, then we denote
$U(T)$ for the set of $T$-valued points {\it over} $S$.
In a formula: $U(T) = \Mor_S(T, U)$.

\medskip\noindent
Note that any fpqc covering is a universal effective
epimorphism, see
Descent, Lemma \ref{descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms}.
Hence the topology on $\Sch_{fppf}$
is weaker than the canonical topology and all representable presheaves
are sheaves.
